summary: Debut analysis video: DHFL bond sale panic drags housing finance stocks; speaker argues capitulation marks a bottom and irrational markets reward skilled traders.
lessons: Markets bottom after big panic selling (capitulation); overreaction to one name often marks a multi-week low.
Panic in one bond/stock drags the whole sector down with it - contagion is mechanical, not fundamental.
Traders who understand irrationality can profit during it; accumulation often starts at maximum pessimism.
quotes: When people are optimistic they will pay the price of a diamond for a pebble; when pessimistic, they will not pay the price of a pebble for a diamond.

summary: Panic morning selling found support at 10,900 (62.8% Fibonacci retracement and Friday low); Nifty shot up 180 points. IndiaBulls Housing Finance crashed ~20% on IL&FS crisis, then rebounded 100+ after IL&FS chairman said all options open to revive it. Bank Nifty swung 10% intraday.
lessons: Markets often bottom after a day of extreme volatility combined with a double bottom.

summary: Powerful short-covering Monday: ICICI Bank's good result and +5% ADR moved sentiment; RBI OMO purchases boosted PSU banks (+8% index); Supreme Court power tariff order lifted power stocks 5-15%; Divi's Labs +15%. Nifty +250 low-to-high, Bank Nifty +600. FII sold 2,300cr, DII bought 2,500cr.
lessons: Markets recover when the last bull turns bear - universal bearishness marks short-term bottoms.

summary: Consolidation with negative bias after US tariff news (Dow -900 intraday). Private banks, Reliance, HDFC dragged; mid/small caps outperformed. FII sold ~1,600cr; October FII selling crossed 30,000cr - highest month since January 2008. India VIX near 21. Bank Nifty flat for 5 weeks despite 500+ point daily swings.
lessons: High VIX with flat close-to-close moves means violent intraday swings inside a range - the option seller's regime map.

summary: Trump's 10% tariff tweet on Chinese phones hit Apple after-hours; Nifty low 10,585, then US-China 'agreed to solve the trade war' headlines lifted US futures and Nifty 70-80 points. HDFC Bank pushed Bank Nifty to a 3-month swing high. OI: 26,000 PE / 26,500 CE. Nifty expiry favored toward the top of 10,500-10,800.
lessons: Trade-war headlines move index futures within minutes - fade confirmation, not the first headline.

summary: VIX masterclass during COVID: definition (expected 30-day movement, not a fear gauge that must rise in falls), sqrt-12 monthly conversion, advance-decline check for why VIX fell on a falling day, and strike placement beyond the expected move.
lessons: VIX measures expected one-month movement; it can fall in a falling market when the fall is narrow (heavyweights only, breadth positive).
Monthly expected move = VIX / sqrt(12); place short strikes beyond that band (example: VIX 60 -> ~17% band).
VIX is derived from option prices - the straddle premium is a live cross-check of the VIX-implied range.
High VIX favors sellers who keep distance; low VIX means the market is priced for calm and strikes must come closer.

strategies.name: VIX-based expected-move strangle placement
strategies.construction: Sell puts below spot - (VIX/sqrt(12))% and calls above spot + (VIX/sqrt(12))%
strategies.numbers: VIX 60 -> monthly band ~17.3%; spot 8,000 -> sell puts below ~6,500, calls above ~9,500; May 8,000 straddle ~1,600 (~20% for 37 trading days)
strategies.best_regime: Elevated VIX (crisis); recompute daily as VIX moves
strategies.adjustments: None stated - guideline framing, refresh band as VIX changes
strategies.risks: Band is statistical, not a wall; theta/other factors shift premiums; violent moves can exceed the band

quotes: It is not necessary that when the market goes down, the VIX has to go up - VIX is all about the perception of the market over the next one month.

summary: First-ever Week Ahead video: 3-session COVID holiday week; India VIX falling; Friday's terrible US jobs data moved Dow only -300 (selling exhaustion); HDFC/ICICI ADRs -8% warn of weak Tuesday open; range 7,500-8,500.
lessons: When bad news moves markets less and less, selling is exhausting - negative impact is limited.
ADR moves of index heavyweights preview Indian bank stocks after holidays.

summary: Against unanimous retail bearishness in COVID: lead-vs-lag indicators, the good/very-good/bad/very-bad news quadrant, consensus danger, efficient markets ('you are last to know'), and why heavy put buying at high premium is a losing game.
lessons: Markets price the lead indicator (next few months) - current bad news is already in the price (efficient market: you are last to know).
Very good news invites profit booking; very bad news invites policy rescue - so both can be sell/buy signals respectively.
Consensus is dangerous: when every retail message is bearish, the short trade is already crowded.
Defensive sectors (FMCG/IT/pharma) can rally through market-worst periods - index-level gloom hides stock-level bull markets.
quotes: Good news is a good news; very good news is a bad news. Bad news is a bad news; very bad news is a good news.
You are the last one to know the fact - whatever is in the public domain is already factored into the market.

summary: COVID-era consolidation: Nifty 8,900-9,100 with heavy volatility; Bank Nifty underperformed. Advance-decline favored advancers despite the fall; VIX rose yet premiums fell (Bank Nifty -400 but weekly 18,000 PE -100). FII AND DII both sold >1,000cr - rare. Weekly OI 8,500 PE / 9,500 CE; monthly support migrating up to 8,200 PE.
lessons: Falling premiums on a down day signal the market does not expect follow-through selling.

summary: P&L transparency episode: ~50% return in six April-2020 sessions driven by VIX collapse 86->50 plus a bullish view; demonstrates position-level losses coexisting with net profit, and strike/expiry diversification; explicitly warns viewers not to copy the risk.
lessons: High-VIX regimes let low-volume sellers earn outsized returns as VIX collapses - the profit engine is vega plus view, not volume.
Spread risk across many strikes (6,500 through 8,500 puts) and multiple expiries (weekly/May/June) - never concentrate one strike.
Position-level losses (up to ~1.75 lakh single positions) coexist with net profit - judge the portfolio, not each leg.
Never copy aggressive sizing: capital and risk appetite differ; matching the trade without matching the capital is ruinous.

strategies.name: Strike-and-expiry put ladder (illustrative, high risk)
strategies.construction: Sold puts at 6,500 / 7,000 / 7,300 / 7,400 / 7,500 / 7,800 / 8,500 across weekly, May and June expiries; small stock-option positions (IndusInd 800 qty @22.52; ~2,300PE on a NBFC stock, 4 lots @220)
strategies.numbers: Capital ~95 lakh -> ~45 lakh profit in 6 sessions (~50%); sold Jun 7,000PE @475, May 6,500PE @210 (closed 80), May 7,000PE @324 (closed 117)
strategies.best_regime: Extreme high VIX with stabilizing market (COVID April 2020)
strategies.adjustments: Laddered entries across expiries instead of single-strike concentration
strategies.risks: Aggressive directional sizing; a renewed crash through the ladder strikes would produce large losses; explicitly not replicable by retail

quotes: We also lose. What matters is whether, at the end of the day, the profits are more than the losses.
I have sold 6,500, 7,000, 7,500, 7,300, 7,400, 7,800, 8,500 - I spread my risk across strike prices and across expiry dates.

summary: PM announced a further 19-day lockdown. Argues the move was 90% expected, so already priced; SGX Nifty traded ~200 points above the India close; herd put-buyers set up for a premium collapse even if prices fell.
lessons: Markets can absorb good or bad news but not uncertainty; once an outcome is known, clarity itself re-prices risk.
When 90% expect a fall, the fall is already priced - consensus trades usually fail.
Option buyers can be right on direction and still lose when uncertainty resolves and premiums collapse.

strategies.name: Multi-strike, multi-expiry put selling (April 2020)
strategies.construction: Sold put options spread across various strike prices and expiry periods rather than one strike
strategies.numbers: 7500PE sold around Rs.75 during a morning dip; SGX Nifty ~9200 vs ~9000 close
strategies.best_regime: Ultra-bearish consensus with the negative surprise already announced
strategies.adjustments: Exited or rolled by expiry; profit disclosed in a later review video
strategies.risks: Losses if the market breaks below the sold strikes; premium is the cap on profit

quotes: Markets can take good news, markets can take bad news, but markets just cannot take the uncertainty.
99 percent of traders lose money, so going with the mass is not a good idea.

summary: Historical framing of gold: price fixed by UK for a century, market data from 1973; three spikes - 1980 Iran revolution/oil crisis, 2008 Lehman, 2020 COVID. Logic: global crisis forces rate cuts, money exits deposits into gold.
lessons: Gold spikes when a global crisis forces central banks to slash rates - near-zero deposit rates make yieldless gold attractive.
Whether to buy gold depends on your view of how long the crisis and the low-rate regime will last.
quotes: Whenever there is a problem faced by the entire world, the gold prices will shoot up.

summary: Explains the historic negative WTI print: contracts marked for physical delivery with storage full forced holders to pay to exit, driving May-2020 futures to -$37 while June contracts stayed normal. Analogy-driven, with explicit disclaimers.
lessons: Contracts expiring into physical delivery can print absurd prices when storage is exhausted - know delivery mechanics before holding.
Negative prices were contract-specific: the next-month contract kept trading at normal positive levels.
quotes: Storage facilities are completely full, no more storage is possible, and that created a huge panic among the buyers.

summary: Builds the case that expert stock-picking barely beats chance: hundreds of coexisting technical methods cannot all work; Malkiel's blindfolded-monkey argument; WSJ dartboard contest (61% expert pick wins, only 51% beat the Dow); 2018 rerun where dart picks returned 17.3% vs experts -4.4% vs S&P +11%.
lessons: If hundreds of technical methods coexist, most cannot work - treat technical analysis as one input, never the system.
In the WSJ decade-long dartboard contest, pros beat the darts 61% of the time but beat the Dow only 51% of the time.
Public picks suffer an announcement effect; experts also skew to high-risk names - both flatter their track records.
quotes: Technical analysis is part of the trading system, not the heart of the trading system.
You look at horoscope also, but you don't marry a girl only by looking at the horoscope.

summary: Two case studies where technicians were trapped: RBI's May 2018 FII window opening in HDFC Bank (cash-futures arb by funds crushed late buyers) and the 2011 flash crash from a broker's basket-order error (Nifty -15% intraday, futures only -3-4%). Conclusion: no single system works.
lessons: Look at everything - news, flows, regulation - never one indicator alone
When a known buying window opens, front-runners buy in cash and short futures; late chart-followers get trapped
Order-entry errors can crash markets 15% in minutes and reverse; stop-losses get hit both ways
If one system reliably worked, everyone would follow it and it would stop working
quotes: No particular system works in the stock market. If any one system worked, everybody would be following that.

summary: Monthly P&L review: April profit 66.3 lakh on ~95 lakh starting capital after 45 lakh in first two weeks; attributes windfall to India VIX collapse 80-85 to ~40 and Nifty clearing the 38.2% Fibonacci retracement (9300-9400) toward 9900-10000; March also +50 lakh selling calls.
lessons: High collapsing VIX plus a clear directional view is where option sellers make windfall profits - not repeatable monthly
Know when to exit: he closed nearly all positions after the Fibonacci target hit
Markets factor in known bad news (efficient market) - shorting after visible bad news is how traders get squeezed
A trader can profit in a falling market and lose in a rising one - the view matters, not the market's direction

strategies.name: Put-selling ladder in collapsing-VIX rebound
strategies.construction: Sold puts across strikes from ~6,100 to 9,000 during April 2020 recovery
strategies.numbers: April profit 66,30,478 on ~95L capital; VIX 80-85 -> 55-60 -> ~40; June 9000PE sold at 500, closed 180
strategies.best_regime: post-crash VIX collapse with market refusing to make new lows
strategies.adjustments: not detailed in this episode
strategies.risks: windfall not repeatable; VIX normalizes; requires conviction view

quotes: A trader can make profit even in a falling market and lose money even in a rising market - it is the view of the trader that is more important.
Markets are irrational and can continue to be irrational until you go bankrupt.

summary: April series ended near highs (~9,850) but weekend brought lockdown extension and zero April auto sales; SGX indicated 500-650 point gap down (worst since March); monthly OI range 9,000-10,500; 10,000 major resistance (Fib 50%).
lessons: May is historically a weak month for equities ('Sell in May') - factor seasonality into OI positioning.
Known-bad data (zero auto sales) is priced in; markets react to surprises, not confirmations.

summary: Two-year Reliance thesis: refinery scale and superior GRMs plus the Jio pivot from commodity to telecom/retail argue for a PE re-rating from ~25 toward 40-50, implying Rs 2,500-3,000; documents the Jio stake-sale wave and the Rs 1,257 rights issue; buy on fundamentals, time on technicals, or use cash-secured puts/SIP.
lessons: Commodity businesses get PE ~10-11; telecom/retail get 40-150+ - business-mix change drives re-rating more than earnings alone.
Choose WHAT to buy from fundamentals; choose WHEN from technicals, cash-secured puts, or SIP.
A decade of flat price followed by breakout can compress years of return into two - equity payoffs are non-linear.
quotes: The biggest risk in your life is not taking any risk.

summary: Century-scale argument against crash calls: 100 years of Dow history shows every major crash (1929 ~90%, dot-com, Lehman) was followed by a powerful rebound; India's 1992/2000/2008/2020 parallels; Nifty PE ~16 sits in the historical buy zone (15-16) vs 28-30 sell zone; advises staggered ETF investing and cash-secured puts; '7500 bottom already made'.
lessons: Markets are unpredictable short-term but mean-revert upward across decades - every crash has been the entry for the next bull.
PE 15-16 has historically been an accumulation zone; 28-30 a distribution zone for Indian indices.
Contrarians win long-term; momentum target-setting is a different game - know which one you are playing.
Prefer broad ETFs over stock-picking unless you can dissect financials.

strategies.name: Staggered index investing with cash-secured puts
strategies.construction: SIP into a Nifty 50 ETF; optionally place cash-secured puts at desired lower entries
strategies.numbers: Nifty PE ~16 (May 2020); historical buy zone 15-16, sell zone 28-30; Dow 1929 crash ~90%; 1982-2000 bull ~15x
strategies.best_regime: Post-crash pessimism; long horizon
strategies.adjustments: Add on further 5-10% falls
strategies.risks: Multi-year drawdowns; requires no-liquidity-needs capital

quotes: A bull market is born out of pessimism, grows out of skepticism, matures out of optimism and dies out of euphoria.

summary: Explains donation-tax mechanics using his charity webinar: PM/CM fund donations get 100% exemption but are capped at 10% of annual profit unless a special COVID ordinance removed the cap for PM Cares; NGO donations only 50%, still 10%-capped; net effect was an extra ~Rs 1.5 lakh personal outflow - 'tax saving is a myth'.
lessons: Donation exemptions cannot shelter trading income: 100% exemption applies only within the 10%-of-profit cap (except the PM Cares ordinance window).
Donations to approved PM/CM funds: 100% deduction; most NGOs: 50% deduction - both subject to the qualifying-limit rule.

summary: Q&A clarifying mechanics: buy/sell quantities are always equal (TV 'delivery buying' is interpretation); futures settle daily via MTM while option sellers' margin = span + premium value, rising with the option price; NSE uses a 10% risk-free rate in IV; June-2020 hedged margins ~one-third of naked; expiry settlement uses last-half-hour weighted average, not last traded price.
lessons: Futures: daily MTM cash transfer. Options: buyer pays premium once; seller's margin floats with the option's price.
Expiry settlement price is the weighted average of the last half hour - an ITM option can expire worthless despite a favorable last traded price.
Hedged option positions carry roughly one-third the margin of naked shorts (June 2020 regime).
Crowd consensus is dangerous: markets are structured so only the minority profits.

summary: Market reaction to the Atmanirbhar package: Nifty broke the key 9,000 support as FIIs sold over Rs 4,000 crore in two sessions; argues the package repackaged earlier announcements with under ~Rs 2 lakh crore true cash outlay and no tax/GST/corporate relief unlike the 2013 playbook; keeps only the market-facts, drops political commentary.
lessons: Announced headline stimulus and actual cash outlay can differ by an order of magnitude - trade the market's verdict, not the headline.
A break of a psychologically important round-number support after a disappointment signals continuation, not opportunity.

summary: Explains the 8,950PE flash spike (0.50 to ~20 in minutes) as a probable fat-finger market buy, citing the earlier NSE episode where a broker's basket-order error crashed Nifty ~15% before reversal; notes May's three weekly expiries all closed within 9,100-9,200 despite violent daily swings; then unpacks why Reliance's rights entitlement traded 30-40 above intrinsic (staggered 25/25/50 payment schedule).
lessons: Resting limit orders far from spot can get filled by flash spikes; square off immediately - such dislocations vanish in seconds and cannot be systematically captured.
A month can be violently volatile intraday yet flat close-to-close: distance-based option selling harvests the chaos.
Staggered-payment instruments (rights entitlements) can rationally trade above intrinsic because of embedded financing value.
quotes: Sometimes the market is like a beach horse: it runs around, but always returns to the same spot.

summary: Monthly trade review: ~10 lakh May profit on ~95 lakh capital (76 lakh total in two months, ~80%). Dissects three large losses (Nifty future and two call options, ~12 lakh combined), a profitable ratio spread, cash-secured puts in ICICI/HDFC Bank, and corrects an earlier mistaken March figure.
lessons: Never benchmark one month against the last - the market 'is like God; take what it gives'. Expectation inflation destroys discipline.
Index-only trading survives regime changes: when SEBI raised stock-option margins from June 2020, index positions kept the margin edge.
Patience through adverse moves rescued the IndusInd straddle: sold at 105, expired with ~80% return despite mid-trade criticism.
Cash-secured puts with genuine willingness to take delivery convert fear into income.

strategies.numbers: +33,000 ICICI and +28,000 HDFC in May 2020
strategies.best_regime: moderately bullish with stocks near support
strategies.adjustments: take delivery if assigned; roll if view changes
strategies.risks: sharp breakdown below strike forces delivery at loss

strategies.construction: Long lower put, short further-OTM puts
strategies.best_regime: mildly bearish to flat
strategies.adjustments: close short side on breakdown
strategies.risks: accelerated loss beyond short strikes

quotes: People lose money because they do not want to lose money - they expect zero-loss calls, which is impossible.

summary: Tax primer: cash-market gains taxed at 15% STCG / 10% LTCG above 1 lakh (post-2018), while F&O profits are business income taxed at slab rates with full expense deduction. Compares individual vs corporate accounts: ~42% top personal rate vs 22-25% corporate, but MAT ~18% limits corporate loss set-off.
lessons: F&O income is business income: slab rates hurt, but expense deduction (broadband, office, salaries, depreciation) and loss set-off often win.
Individual accounts can carry trading losses forward ~8 years against future profits; corporate accounts face MAT (~18%) even in profit years, limiting set-off value.
Entity choice rule of thumb: large, consistently profitable capital -> corporate (22-25% vs ~42%); small capital or loss-prone -> individual.
Cash-market capital gains allow no expense deduction - flat 15%/10% - unlike business income.
quotes: Go and make profit first, then come to me - the auditor's answer to every F&O tax question.

summary: Bullish call vindicated: Nifty 9,000->10,200 in ~7 sessions as FIIs turned daily buyers; US May payrolls +2.5M vs -8M expected sent Nasdaq to ATH; recounts Nov-2018 elections->Balakot FII cycle; NSE option-price glitch Thursday hurt traders.
lessons: Don't be a bull or a bear - be a chameleon; markets change trend when everyone leans one way.
Always trade with the trend; fighting it with leverage (F&O) makes losses heavy.

summary: Euphoric gap-up morning (Nifty +200, Bank Nifty +500) fizzled: pre-market blog call that Nifty future would break 10,200 at least once played out; session closed as a Doji via the weighted-average close; RBI nod for IndusInd open-market buys lifted it early while HDFC/Kotak/Reliance were sold hard from highs; FII +813 cr vs DII -1,238 cr; view: consolidation with positive bias, supports 9,900/9,700.
lessons: Euphoric gaps attract profit-booking: 'a bull market dies of euphoria' - fade the open, respect the close.
The printed close is a last-half-hour weighted average - comparing it to yesterday's true close can fake a 'Doji' or fake momentum.
When a stock sets all-time highs and is still sold into strength, the positives are priced - supply beats narrative.
Stated supports belong to risk classes: 9,900 for aggressive traders, 9,700 for moderate - sizing follows the classification.
quotes: A bull market is born out of pessimism, grows out of skepticism, matures out of optimism and dies out of euphoria.

summary: US reality-check week: Nasdaq ATH despite 2M+ infections; Fed caution sent US -7% Thursday; Nifty closed ~10,000 Friday instead of feared crash (already -2% Thursday; Asia only -1-2%); IIP -55% (lockdown); consolidation 9,500-10,500.
lessons: Relative positioning logic: if you already fell 2% and Asia only falls 1-2% after a US -7% night, the gap-down gets bought.
Already-corrected markets have less downside from a global shock - fresh shorting invites short covering.

summary: Builds a limited-risk call ratio on the post-COVID rally: buy 1x 10,500 Aug CE @360, sell 3x 11,000 Aug CE, buy 2x 11,500 Aug CE; net credit ~1,900; margin ~63,000 effective; max profit ~37,000 at Nifty 11,000; breakeven 11,253; max loss ~37,000 above 11,500; anchored on 200-DMA + 50% Fibonacci resistance.
lessons: Turn a 'resistance holds' view into a credit ratio spread; add far calls to cap the unlimited-risk tail.
Net-credit gating: if the structure is a debit in the near expiry, step out to the far month where it pays you.
Margin-benefit rules let 2-3 lakh accounts run defined-risk ratio structures.

summary: Q&A: blue-chip etymology from casino chips; SLB as delivery backstop; American vs European styles and assignment risk; no exchange-resident stop-loss for delivery trades in India; breakeven limits unknowable pre-expiry; long-term patience (Reliance flat 2008-17, then 3.5x); discretionary trading produced best and worst single days (±10% of capital).
lessons: 'Blue chip' comes from the casino's highest-value chip - the term predates markets.
No exchange-held stop-loss for delivery positions in India; brokers simulate GTC by re-placing daily.
Reliance went nowhere 2008-2017 then rose ~3.5x by 2020: equity returns are lumpy; patience is structural.
Discretionary trades on violent days produced both the best (+10% of capital in a day) and worst (-10%) single-day outcomes.
quotes: Equity needs patience: some stocks give ten years of return in the last two years.

summary: Reconciles a Reliance long-futures position: June 2020 rally from 1460 to 1784 gave ~3 lakh stock profit, but total P&L of 592,592 (as of Friday) came from an options overlay - sold-call ladders plus a straddle conversion. An error trade (call sold instead of put) forced doubled corrective legs and ~30 adjustment trades.
lessons: Hedging a directional position with short calls can outperform the stock itself - profit doubled versus holding the future alone.
One mis-executed leg (call instead of put) forced doubling of offsetting legs and heavy margin strain - verify every leg at entry.
Violent single-stock moves demand many small adjustments; firefighting is workload, not genius.

strategies.name: Hedged long stock/futures with call ladder + straddle conversion
strategies.construction: Long 2 lots (1000 shares) Reliance futures from ~1010; sold 1580/1600/1640/1680/1700 calls progressively; converted a 1500 short call into a short straddle by selling 1500 puts (later doubled after error)
strategies.numbers: June: stock +~3,00,000; options overlay +~2,90,000; total 592,592 at month-end week; ~30 trades executed
strategies.best_regime: Strongly trending large-cap you want to hold; sell calls above trend to monetize drift
strategies.adjustments: Rolled sold calls up the ladder as price ran; doubled puts after leg error; kept net long exposure
strategies.risks: Gap above highest sold call caps upside; margin spikes when doubling corrective legs

quotes: if the market goes down, we make money in call options... the idea is to outperform the stock itself
this is the power of hedging

summary: Q&A batch: STT mechanics on sellers; time decay proportional to expiry (weekly day-1 = 20% of decay, expiry day = 100%); covered calls against physical shares still need full margin in India (no cash-F&O link) but a long futures leg reduces it to exposure margin; Bharat Bond 1 vs 2 (yield, premium, pledge-ability delay); NSE's six-month co-location ban on new contracts had just ended; bear/bull defined by 20% thresholds.
lessons: Time decay is proportional to remaining time: a one-week option loses ~20% of its value on day one, but ~100% on expiry day - expiry-day selling harvests decay that weekly sellers spread across days.
India charges full span+exposure margin on covered calls against demat shares (no cash-F&O link); holding a long future instead cuts the short call's span to zero - only exposure margin applies.
An instrument's 'maximum loss' framing: any investment can lose 100%; relative safety comes from the borrower (Bharat Bond lends only to public-sector enterprises).
Bond yields falling means older bonds trade at a premium (Bharat Bond 1 near 1080-1090 vs 1000 face); pledging older listed bonds can beat waiting for new issues to clear collateral approval.

strategies.name: Covered call via futures leg (margin-optimized)
strategies.construction: Hold long futures instead of physical shares; sell calls against it
strategies.numbers: Stated: span margin zero for the covered call against long futures; exposure margin ~2% index, ~3.5% stock options
strategies.best_regime: Large holders wanting option income without physical-settlement complexity
strategies.adjustments: Roll calls up as futures rally
strategies.risks: Futures MTM swings; margin calls if exposure margin rules change

strategies.construction: Pledge Liquid BeES/debt funds (~90% collateral value); keep a small cash buffer for debit legs
strategies.numbers: Buy-side premium debits settle immediately; sell-side credits arrive next day - keep cash for combos
strategies.best_regime: All option sellers using collateral
strategies.adjustments: Top up cash before multi-leg strategies
strategies.risks: Settlement timing on multi-leg entries; penalty on shortfall

quotes: when running a casino is more profitable, why do people choose to be gamblers?
time decay will be proportional to the expiry time

summary: Counters technical analysts calling for a 7500 retest: after the October 2008 Lehman low (2252), Nifty doubled within a year and the low was never retested; the COVID candle's high was 11400 - once crossed, it may never be retested. COVID fell less than 50% (vs 2008's >50%), so recovery may be slower, but 15000 arrives before 7500. Investment timing: invest when you have surplus cash; exit when you need the money.
lessons: Post-crash lows of true panic candles (2008, 2020) are historically not retested once the recovery candle's high is crossed - drawdown bottoming behaves asymmetrically.
The depth of the crash sets the pace of recovery: 2008's >50% fall doubled in a year; 2020's shallower fall implies a slower but persistent recovery.
The right time to invest is when you have surplus cash; the right time to exit is when you need the money - waiting for the 'right opportunity' is itself a losing strategy.
quotes: the right time to invest is when you have surplus cash. The right time to exit is when you need the money

summary: Counters the 'invest for long term' reflex: Nifty top-50 averaged ~11x over 1994-2020 (doubling slower than 6 years) while risk-free debt doubled in ~6; only stock-pickers or entry-exit timers should invest; Anil Ambani group stocks lost 95-99%.
lessons: Nifty top-50 average return 1994-2020 did not double in 6 years, underperforming risk-free debt instruments doubling in ~6.
Index survivorship inflates returns: failing companies are ejected, so you average only the winning horses.
Stock market suits only stock-pickers or those who time entries and exits; passive buy-and-hold is sold as a myth.
quotes: Stock market is only for two people: those who can pick the stock that performs, or those who know when to get in and out.

summary: Defends the 15000-before-7500 call: consensus is dangerous (99% polled bearish, market rallied); Nifty PE 28 is not a fixed top because Rule-of-72 FD doubling moved 9->18 years, tripling justifiable PE; dividend-yield screen says market is skeptical, not euphoric.
lessons: Consensus is dangerous: when 99% expect a fall, markets climb the wall of worry.
Justifiable PE scales inversely with interest rates - with FD doubling in 18 years (4%), a 3x premium implies PE far above the historic 28 top.
Euphoria screen: if no Nifty-50 stock yields more than bank FDs, the market is euphoric; in 2020 ITC/ONGC/IOC/GAIL/Vedanta yielded above FDs, so the stage was skepticism.
Markets never move in straight lines - give direction calls a horizon, not a deadline.
quotes: Bull market is born out of pessimism, grows out of skepticism, matures out of optimism and dies out of euphoria.

summary: P&L showcase: claims Rs 1.05 cr profit April-July 2020 on Rs 95 L capital (~110% in 4 months), Rs 66L April / Rs 10L May / -Rs 1.2L June / Rs 31L July; also claims Rs 47L profit during the March 2020 crash and Rs 1.55 cr over 10 months; closes with troll-defense and workshop-review promotion.
lessons: Option selling is a book of many trades: a few failures drown in the aggregate profit - the insurance-pool principle.
Adjustments and firefighting (not stop-losses) are how a losing view becomes a small profit or small loss.
Personal P&L screenshots are marketing, not evidence: audit capital trajectory and consistency, not single screenshots (inversion of the scam test).
quotes: I am not the god, I am just good.

summary: Explains SEBI's cash-market margin changes effective 1 August 2020: upfront margin now required even to sell shares already held, because the exchange cannot distinguish intraday sells from delivery sells. Walks through VaR+ELM+additional margin arithmetic (Reliance ~22%, SBI ~35%, Idea ~77.5%), T+2 settlement, early pay-in, and the auction market for short deliveries; predicts movement toward T+1.
lessons: Intraday margin scales with stock volatility: roughly 4.5x leverage on Reliance (~22%) but barely 1.3x on Idea (~77.5%) at the time.
From August 2020, selling shares you already hold also requires margin in the account - the exchange cannot tell an intraday sell from a delivery sell.
Settlement mechanics: T-day trade, T+1 funds/shares to broker/exchange, T+2 demat/money transfer; early pay-in avoids the shortfall but forfeits the auction-market rescue for short deliveries.
A broker without early pay-in can cover a client's accidental short delivery via the auction market - the auction price risk falls on the client.
quotes: Anything that cannot be liquidated immediately cannot be given as a collateral.

summary: Reliance long-futures case study: entry ~1400 (May 2020), price ~2000 by 3 August 2020. Pure cash-market hold would have made ~6 lakh; dynamic hedging and firefighting made ~13.1 lakh in the main account plus 8 lakh+ in a second account (~21-22 lakh total), though 40-50 lakh extra margin was injected. Detailed adjustment ladder: sold 1800/1900/2000 calls, rolled to 2040/2100, sold 2180 call, bought 1700 put (over 1 lakh loss), sold puts 1680 down to 1400, then aggressively sold 1900-2200 puts (12.66 lakh from put selling in July).
lessons: A hedged directional position can triple a plain cash-market gain (6L -> ~21-22L) - but only with margin headroom (40-50L extra injected here).
Firefighting ladder on a runaway trend: sell calls above, roll them up as the trend extends, then fund the ride by selling puts below the market.
Accept small planned losses inside the ladder: the 1700 protective put lost over 1 lakh while the overall program stayed heavily profitable.
'Only two lots' became a much larger exposure through firefighting - position growth must be a conscious choice, not an accident.

strategies.name: Reliance long futures + rolling option ladder
strategies.construction: Long 2 lots futures (~1000 shares @~1400); short 1800/1900/2000CE rolled to 2040/2100CE then 2180CE; long 1700PE; short 1680/1640/1600/1500/1400PE; later aggressive short 1900-2200PE
strategies.numbers: 13.12L profit (main account, incl. 12.66L from July put selling + 84k August); ~8L+ second account; ~40-50L additional margin deployed
strategies.best_regime: Strong vertical uptrend with high IV ( premium selling on both sides)
strategies.adjustments: Roll short calls up strike by strike; convert to put selling below market once trend confirmed; accept small hedge losses
strategies.risks: Deep gap reversal against both legs; escalating margin needs; overconfidence after wins

quotes: Many people think you have to trade too much to make profit, but here I traded only two lots.

summary: Critique of SEBI's peak-margin framework: intraday leverage phased out (from Dec 1 2020, brokers could offer only ~3x, then 1x, then ~0.25x, ultimately none by around August-September 2021); margin must cover peak intraday MTM exposure, penalized 0.5%/1% per day on shortages. Highlights unfairness of freak trades (a single 10,800 print vs 11,000 Nifty) creating phantom MTM losses, and argues SEBI restricts option sellers while the real speculators are option buyers - the drunkard-searching-under-the-streetlight analogy.
lessons: Peak-margin logic: your account must fund the worst intraday MTM excursion, not just the closing position - violent days create penalty risk even if the day ends flat.
The phase-out calendar (Dec 2020: ~3x intraday limit; +3 months: ~1x; +3 months: ~0.25x; by Aug-Sep 2021: none) forced the end of 10x-100x broker leverage.
Freak trades printing far below market can fabricate MTM drawdowns; without an exemption, honest accounts eat penalties for trades they never faced.
Regulatory asymmetry: curbs concentrated on option sellers (who post big margins) while option buyers - the actual gamblers - face no new restrictions.
quotes: Sometimes SEBI behaves like the man who lost his ring in the dark but searches under the streetlight because the light is there.

summary: Gold crashed 6% in a day (silver -15%) days after Russia's COVID-vaccine announcement, from its ~$2,070 all-time high. Historical frame: gold's three modern spikes (1980 oil crisis $200->$600+, 2008 Lehman $700->$1900, 2020 COVID $1200->$2000+) all came with global crises and collapsing rates; the 2011 peak was followed by a one-day 10% crash and a slide to $1070. Argues $2070 will not be revisited until the next systemic crisis; notes rotation from new-economy to old-economy stocks, and that markets rise when everybody is bearish. Personal book: 60-70 lakh in December 2020 index options gaining ~1 lakh/day for three days (+3%) as IV fell 30->20; buy 400-500 point Nifty dips.
lessons: Gold's modern spikes map to global crises (1980 oil shock, 2008 Lehman, 2020 COVID) - it is a fear asset, not a return asset.
Gold's all-time highs get made during systemic crises and can take decades to revisit (1980 peak held until 2008; post-2011 high ran to $1070).
Vaccine/normalization news deflates the fear premium: metals crashed the day after Russia's August 2020 vaccine announcement while old-economy stocks with 'bad results' rallied.
Falling IV collapses both call and put premiums - long-dated option buyers harvest theta-and-IV decay; position for IV regime, not direction alone.

strategies.name: Long-dated index option buying on IV collapse
strategies.construction: Deployed 60-70 lakh across December 2020 Nifty options (puts and calls), holding 30-40 lakh cash for adjustments
strategies.numbers: +~1 lakh/day for three consecutive days (~3% on deployed capital) as IV fell from ~30 to ~20
strategies.best_regime: Post-panic IV compression with market stabilization
strategies.adjustments: Keep 30-40% dry powder for adjustments
strategies.risks: Time decay if IV stays low and market ranges; long options bleed without direction

quotes: When the whole world is facing a big problem, that is when the gold prices will shoot up.
If you ask me the single most important reason why markets are bullish - because everybody is bearish.

summary: ADR explainer anchored on ICICI Bank's 10 August 2020 QIP: targeted 15,000 crore, drew ~62,000 crore (4x+ oversubscribed); the ADR rose ~4% overnight, so Bank Nifty puts were sold next morning for profit. Explains ADR mechanics and ratios (HDFC Bank ADR = 3 shares, ICICI = 2, Tata Motors = 4, Vedanta = 5), why HDFC Bank's ADR traded ~10% premium (FII ownership limit exhausted, so US buyers pay up rather than hit the India cap), and notes GDRs in London (Reliance).
lessons: ADR overnight moves are a reliable next-day read-through for most large caps - the same global holders reprice the Indian line at open.
ADR ratios vary (1 ADR = 2-5 Indian shares); convert properly before comparing prices.
When FII ownership hits the sectoral cap, arbitrage breaks: the ADR can hold a 10% premium indefinitely because FIIs cannot buy more in India - so the premium is information, not free money.
QIPs at huge oversubscription signal institutional demand and often predate strength in the stock.
quotes: ADRs are the Indian shares which are being traded in US stock exchanges.

summary: Mechanics of the F&O ban (Market Wide Position Limit): MWPL = 20% of free-float market cap; a stock enters ban when combined open interest ends a day above 95% of MWPL; no fresh F&O positions next day (existing positions square-off only); ban lifts only when OI falls below 80%. Penalty for banned trading: 1% of contract value or 5,000 rupees, whichever is higher, capped at 1 lakh/day. Live examples: Vodafone Idea at 93.5% utilization, Canara Bank in ban at 88.5% (descending), Adani Enterprises at 88% not banned; nine stocks in ban for 12 August 2020.
lessons: MWPL math: 20% of free-float market cap caps total F&O open interest; speculative smallcaps hit it far sooner than large caps.
Ban asymmetry: entry at 95% utilization but exit only below 80% - ban lists persist for days and freeze hedgers mid-position.
During a ban you can only square off: no fresh futures or options positions, so adjustment trades become impossible exactly when risk peaks.
Trading a banned stock costs at least 5,000 rupees per lot (1% of contract value), capped at 1 lakh per day - plus unquantifiable exit-liquidity risk.
quotes: Usually the stocks that come under trading ban are the highly speculative stocks.

summary: Pair trading as a market-neutral structure: long one instrument, short another (often same sector, e.g., long HDFC/ICICI vs short SBI/BoB; long Maruti vs short Tata Motors). COVID example: Maruti -33% while Tata Motors -85% made the pair hugely profitable. Live demonstration with Nifty long / Bank Nifty short across one week, two weeks and one month (Aug 2020) showing positive net P&L in all three windows as Nifty outperformed (10,200 -> ~11,300 while Bank Nifty crawled 21,500 -> 21,800).
lessons: Pair trading isolates relative strength: you profit from the spread between two instruments, not from market direction - gaps and crashes largely cancel.
Classic pairs: private banks long vs PSU banks short; quality autos long vs weak autos short; index long vs lagging index short.
Spread math dominates: when Nifty rose ~1,100 points while Bank Nifty rose ~300, the long-Nifty/short-BankNifty pair collected the differential on both legs.
Divergent beta is the edge and the risk: in a crash the 'strong' leg can fall just as hard - pairs are hedged, not riskless ('fail proof' is sales talk).

strategies.name: Nifty long / Bank Nifty short pair
strategies.construction: Long 1 lot Nifty futures + short 1 lot Bank Nifty futures (25 lot size), rebalanced views weekly
strategies.numbers: One-week window: ~4,725 loss on Nifty leg vs ~12,775 profit on Bank Nifty leg; two-week window: net ~12,000+ profit; one-month window positive
strategies.best_regime: Index divergence phases - Bank Nifty underperforming Nifty for weeks
strategies.adjustments: Re-evaluate pair weekly; exit when the spread normalizes
strategies.risks: Correlation breakdown in crashes; both legs can lose if sized wrong; margin on two futures legs

quotes: Pair trading means going long in one stock and going short in another - the differential profit is your profit.

summary: Introduces MCX BULLDEX bullion-index futures launched 24 Aug 2020: 70.52% gold / 29.48% silver weights, lot 50, monthly expiry, price ~16,000, contract ~8 lakh, margin ~6% (~48,000), tick 1. Frames gold as an inverse-correlation hedge and a pair-trading complement to equity positions.
lessons: Gold moves opposite equities over long cycles - 2008-2011 gold rose >400% post-Lehman while stocks crashed; 2020 COVID gold nearly doubled from the bottom.
A 10-20% bullion exposure lets equity shorts/longs be paired against gold positions as a cross-asset hedge.
New futures instruments can hedge equity portfolios at ~6% margin versus costly physical gold or gold ETFs.

strategies.name: Bullion index equity hedge
strategies.construction: Long/short equity portfolio paired with same-direction or inverse position in MCX BULLDEX futures (70.52% gold / 29.48% silver)
strategies.numbers: lot 50; ~16,000 index; ~8 lakh contract value; ~6% margin (~48,000); tick 1
strategies.best_regime: Portfolio-level diversification when equity-gold inverse correlation is intact
strategies.adjustments: Rebalance weights as gold/silver ratio drifts; roll monthly expiry
strategies.risks: Correlation breakdown; VaR-driven margin changes

quotes: When the markets are in bull mode, the gold will be in a bear mode. When the markets are in bear mode, the gold will be in a bull mode.

summary: Explains the COVID loan-moratorium interest-waiver case before the Supreme Court after the six-month EMI holiday: banks argue depositors must be paid; borrowers seek interest waiver. Three outcomes: government compensates banks (ruled out - Centre denied), borrowers pay full interest, or reduced interest covering bank cost. Bank Nifty fell 2,000+ in a week on this uncertainty.
lessons: Policy overhangs (court cases, regulatory decisions) create sector-specific drag - Bank Nifty underperformed while awaiting the moratorium verdict.
Bank economics frame: deposits at ~5%, loans at ~8%; waiving borrower interest breaks the deposit-obligation chain unless someone pays.
Clarity itself is a catalyst - sectors recover once uncertainty resolves, whatever the direction.
quotes: Whenever US markets went up, we did not go up. But whenever US markets were going down, we were falling.

summary: After Nifty corrected 11,800 to ~11,200 and Bank Nifty 3,000+, asks crash vs correction: March 2020 crashed with VIX spiking 15 to 85; this fall came without a VIX spike or negative news - US tech profit-booking (Tesla -21%, Apple -6%, Dow -650, Nasdaq into correction). Newton's first law framing: falls continue till an external force (big buyer) intervenes; bought ITC averaging down at 183.
lessons: Crash requires a VIX spike tied to negative news; a fall without VIX expansion is profit booking and tends to stabilize.
Newton's first law for markets: trends persist until an external force - watch for the big buy order that arrests a fall.
Once a 15-30% correction makes prices attractive, new buyers arrive and markets stabilize - sell-offs without news are opportunities, not exits.
quotes: If the bigger crash has to come, the volatility index has to shoot up. Right now it is not shooting up as much as people are expecting.

summary: DXY primer: a 1973-vintage index of dollar strength vs six currencies (EUR 57.6%, JPY 13.6%, GBP 11.9%, CAD 9.1%, SEK 4.2%, CHF 3.6%), changed only once (DEM to EUR). Below 100 = weak dollar, above = strong; 1985 peak 165, Lehman-era low ~70, then ~93. Sub-93 DXY historically coincides with rising Indian markets.
lessons: The dollar index is a 50-year-old six-currency basket whose weights no longer match US trade - a good cue, not gospel.
Sub-100 dollar strength thresholds are the flag to watch for emerging-market flow direction.
quotes: If the dollar index is below 100 the dollar is weakening; above 100 it is strengthening.

summary: ITC at ~₹180 with 5.5%+ yield still falls despite universal analyst backing: ESG screens (tobacco) exclude it for funds, and the 2020 dividend-tax flip (DDT ~20% abolished; dividends taxed at slab, ~42% for ultra-HNI) cut post-tax yield from ₹100 to ₹70 per ₹120 - chilling HNI demand for yield stocks.
lessons: ESG screens are a structural demand hole for certain sectors - a cheap stock can stay cheap because mandated money cannot buy it.
Tax regimes decide yield-stock demand: shifting dividend tax from company (DDT) to recipient slab cut effective yields ~30% for top-bracket holders.
quotes: A cheap stock can stay cheap because the big money is simply not allowed to buy it.

summary: The Robinhood phenomenon mapped to India: 300% jump in Zerodha's new demat accounts, 2.6M CDSL accounts since March (record 8,30,405 in June vs ~3L/month in FY20), retail at 68% of cash volumes - a decade high. Cautionary anchor: Nikkei 40,000 (1989) still ~half after 30 years; Shanghai never reclaimed its pre-Lehman 6,000 in 12 years; skills before size.
lessons: Record account openings mark euphoria tops more than opportunities - the wave that lifts markets also supplies its exits.
A market can stay below its high for decades (Nikkei 1989, Shanghai 2007) - 'it always comes back' is survivorship folklore.
Acquire skill before size: the lockdown cohort learned trading from YouTube tutorials with pandemic savings.
quotes: The market can stay below its peak for thirty years - make sure you acquire skills before you commit money.

summary: Trump's COVID hospitalization is the global wildcard; Friday's Bank Nifty short-covering lifted markets near 11,450; interest-on-interest affidavit (government pays for loans up to 2 crore) already priced; FIIs flipped to buying; range 10,800-11,600 pending US president's health.
lessons: Verdicts pre-leaked via affidavits become non-events; watch what is already factored, not the calendar.
Presidential-health risk demands wide option ranges - sizing the band to the tail-risk, not the quiet tape.

summary: Post-market analysis of a 300-point Nifty fall: Supreme Court loan-moratorium interest-on-interest uncertainty hit Bank Nifty (-1,150 from high), US stimulus stalemate, France/UK COVID restrictions; uses Sep-24 expiry analog to frame next-day scenarios and S&P 500 VIX ~29-30 as exit trigger.
lessons: Policy uncertainty without a verdict is what markets fear; the RBI/Supreme Court moratorium case kept banks under pressure
HDFC Bank's index weightage is so large that a 10-rupee move shifts Bank Nifty ~200 points
Compare the current session to a recent structurally similar session (Sep-24 expiry) to script next-day scenarios
When S&P 500 VIX crosses ~30, it is time to close positions
quotes: If S&P 500 VIX is crossing 30, then it is time to close the positions

summary: Binary events explained (coin toss; Sholay joke). Nifty crossed 12,000 then fell 250 points (Bank Nifty -750) as Europe's COVID resurgence and the missed US stimulus deadline hit; 80% recovered intraday. October data: VIX rose in 8 of 14 sessions. FII +2,100cr (5,000cr in 3 days), DII -1,600cr. Reliance weak vs HDFC strength; double-top risk noted; 12,400 next if 12,000 breaks.
lessons: Binary events raise VIX and premiums in both directions - fear is not only downside fear.

summary: Consolidation at ~11,900 for five straight sessions after the 1,200-point surge; results-packed expiry week (~30% of Nifty reporting incl. RIL, ICICI, Kotak); negatives: DII selling, stalled US stimulus, Europe COVID surge; expects 250-300 point expiry move, tilt higher; range 11,600-12,200.
lessons: Post-surge consolidation (2-3 weeks) precedes a significant expiry-week move - the pattern repeats month after month.
Stocks down heavily into results often see short-covering rallies; stocks up hugely into results see profit-booking.

summary: Week fell 400 points on European lockdowns and stalled stimulus; US election is the year's biggest event - contested outcome is the only bearish case; option premiums ultra-high (Bank Nifty ATM straddle ~2,000); advice: no directional trades until results; investors split 50/50 entries.
lessons: Markets want stability, not a party: any clear US winner lifts stocks; only a contested result sells them off.
Before binary events, keep traders out and let investors scale in 50/50 - insurance via position structure, not prediction.

summary: Nifty took out its all-time high (~12,427) on Biden's election clarity, FII inflows of 10,000cr in two sessions, MSCI rebalancing (~18,000cr) and Pfizer-BioNTech's >90% vaccine efficacy. Lead-vs-lag indicator doctrine; retail 85% short, FII 75% short in F&O yet cash buyers; HDFC Bank FII-limit arbitrage story; bus-pothole lesson on copying big players; Bank Nifty still ~4,000-5,000 below its ATH.
lessons: Markets price the lead indicator six months ahead, not today's lagging data.

summary: RCEP trade pact (15 nations, ~25% of world GDP) signed without fanfare lifted Asian markets; Biden's no-nationwide-lockdown line, strong Japan GDP and China data added fuel; CPI/WPI highs shrugged off as lag indicators; bears 'hibernating'; range 12,400-13,000 in truncated week.
lessons: Lead indicators (policy, stimulus, reopening) move markets; lag indicators (CPI/WPI prints) get shrugged off in uptrends.
Big positive agreements often arrive quietly - headlines, not handshakes, move markets.

summary: Deepavali year-ahead forecast: shows 2008-2020 was the longest consolidation (Nifty 6,000->12,000; under 1%/yr in dollar terms), so the next leg should be a bull run; COVID dip = the pre-jump 'monkey dip'; VIX ~20 implies ±20% band; predicts Nifty 15,500 by next Deepavali.
lessons: Twelve years of consolidation after 2008 set up the 2020s bull leg - long stagnation resolves upward in a cycle framework
FIIs judge India in dollars: rupee depreciation halved their 2008-2020 return to ~1%/yr
India VIX ≈ the market's expected ±move over a month; extrapolate cautiously for longer horizons
Bull runs start with a dip-then-launch pattern; a right-curve dip is fuel, not failure
quotes: People who are trading in futures have no future; people trading in options have plenty of options - but a bull run needs a dip first: the monkey dips before it jumps

summary: Case study of Lakshmi Vilas Bank: RBI wrote off equity and mandated DBS takeover on Nov 17, 2020, yet retail kept buying the falling stock through lower circuits until delisting on Nov 25 - the informed profit at the expense of the uninformed; lesson: research before buying collapsed stocks.
lessons: When RBI writes off a bank's equity, the share's value is zero regardless of how cheap it looks - falling 20% twice is not a discount
Follow the news chain before buying a distressed stock; a circuit-down price is not a sale tag
Nobody will protect you - not the exchange, which let trading continue for days after the write-off decision
Markets transfer money from the uninformed to the informed; do your own research or pay tuition
quotes: Stock market is where people with money meet people with experience - then the experienced become rich and the rich become experienced

summary: Nifty hits fresh all-time high; debunks MSCI-rebalancing explanation (global peers rallied more), credits global liquidity (DXY<91), vaccine hope; heavyweight recovery thesis; FII/DII flows and option-chain OI read; sold puts into the rally.
lessons: Ride the trend: as long as the rally is on, stay with it - do not predict its end.
Judge rallies by global breadth, not a single excuse like index rebalancing.
Heavyweight lag (Reliance/HDFC ~25% of Nifty) hiding strength signals upside when they catch up.
Max-OI put addition below price = firm bull grip; call unwinding confirms.
quotes: A bull market is born out of pessimism, grows out of skepticism, matures out of optimism and dies out of euphoria.
So as long as the rally is there, we ride the rally - that should be a trader's mentality.

summary: IPO vs OFS explainer: IPO money goes to the company; OFS is an existing shareholder (Government) selling. Walks through applying via a broker's online console (corporate actions > OFS > cutoff price for retail <2 lakh). IRCTC context: 2019 IPO at 320, rallied ~600% to ~2,000, OFS floor 1,367.
lessons: In an OFS the company gets nothing - an existing shareholder is exiting, so the process and risks differ from an IPO.
Retail applicants (<2 lakh) should bid at cutoff price to avoid being priced out.
A hot prior IPO listing does not guarantee OFS profits - IRCTC had corrected ~15% into the OFS.
quotes: An OFS is one shareholder offering his shares for sale - the company does not receive the money.

summary: Rally broadening: Nifty crossed 13,500 (future high 13,599); FII December inflows ~3,000 crore/day (record Friday 4,500 crore); vaccine news-flow analogy (one good news repeating daily); sector rotation day-by-day (PSU banks +7% index day, FMCG, energy); tactic: sell 13,000PE on 100-point intraday falls; range 13,200-13,800.
lessons: One good news recurs daily like bad news did in the crash - narrative tails (vaccine, stimulus) extend trends.
When flat indices mask 7% sector-index days, the rally is rotating and intact; 'trend is your friend until it bends'.

summary: Pre-launch explainer for Nifty Financial Services derivatives (launched 11 Jan 2021): 20 banks/insurers/NBFCs; beta 1.2 between Nifty (1.0) and Bank Nifty (1.36); 94% correlation to Nifty, 98% to Bank Nifty; contract size 40 (~5.5-6 lakh notional), 3 monthly + 7 weekly contracts, expiry last Thursday, strike interval 100, freeze qty 5,001.
lessons: Sector index design: FinNifty was built as the middle risk point between Nifty and Bank Nifty.
Contract size sets the margin ticket - a smaller notional index lowers the entry barrier.
Correlation stats (94%/98%) tell you a new index is not true diversification within the same family.
FII flows concentrated in financials (35% of holdings, ~48% of incremental flows) justified a financials index.

summary: Nifty P/E hit a record 37.16 (P/B 3.82, dividend yield 1.18). Argues crash calls from P/E alone are wrong: P/E = price/EPS, and COVID-crushed EPS inflated the ratio. P/E can normalize via falling prices OR recovering earnings - shows Maruti EPS -8 to +46, ONGC collapse; if earnings double, P/E halves without any fall.
lessons: P/E has two levers: price and earnings; focusing on only one while predicting crashes is a category error.
Distressed EPS makes P/E meaningless (zero/negative earnings = infinite P/E at any price).
A ratio can normalize without a crash if earnings recover - the 2020 P/E spike was a denominator artifact.
Trend is your friend until it bends: do not short a market merely because a single valuation metric is stretched.
quotes: A ratio with two parameters cannot be judged by watching one - people watch price and ignore earnings.

summary: New UK COVID strain crashed global markets; Nifty fell >3%, Bank Nifty >4%, mid/smallcaps >5% on profit-booking cascade. Advised selling calls into panic, shopping for high-dividend stocks as investor, and waiting before calling trend reversal.
lessons: Bull-market corrections are fast and furious; two steps up, one step down.
In panic, sell calls aggressively (premiums are rich) while investors shop for dividend stocks.

summary: December 2020: after a 3,000-point Nifty rally (Sept expiry ~10,800 to ~13,800) and ~50% Bank Nifty rally (~10,000 points), the speaker frames the 5 Jan 2021 Georgia US Senate runoffs as the global make-or-break event: divided vs unified government determines stimulus flow.
lessons: Divided US government stalls fiscal stimulus and keeps global markets uncertain; unified government (with VP tie-break) can unlock a fresh rally leg.
A single pending election can be the hinge on which an extended bull market's next leg swings.
quotes: The same way, in US, they have House and Senate... a lot of bills got delayed.

summary: COVID-strain Monday: Nifty >500 intraday fall, Bank Nifty −1,500, then three-day rebound; week closed near prior close. Year-end: FII volumes −30–40%, holiday lull. OI: 13,500 PE / 14,000 CE max. Brexit deal done. Range call 13,500–14,000; sold calls >14,000, puts <13,500.
lessons: Bull-market corrections are fast and furious — and can recover with the same speed.
Holiday-week volume is insignificant, so price action in it should also be treated as insignificant.

summary: All-time-high day (~13,900 future) after Brexit deal signed, Trump signed stimulus, vaccine-efficiency news. Delivered the 'everything people do in the market is wrong' monologue: no training culture, 'which share will go up?', 95% failure ignored, business has no predetermined stop-loss.
lessons: Nobody starts a restaurant with a predetermined stop-loss - diagnose, adjust, and only quit when it is genuinely not your cup of tea.
95% of investors and 99% of traders lose, yet everyone wants to trade - question the base rate before entering.

summary: Defines the three market cycles - bull, bear and sideways ('bunny') - and price correction vs time correction; shows Nifty 2003-07 4-6x bull, then 2008-2020 as India's longest consolidation where even 13 years of index gains lost to bank FDs; Chennai builder parable about exploiting cycle ignorance.
lessons: Sideways markets are a 'time correction' - with opportunity cost included, flat index years can underperform bank FDs.
2003-2007 delivered a 4-7x bull; 2008-2020 was the longest consolidation in Indian market history - cycles, not linearity, are the norm.
Only experts capture cycle turning points (builder parable): amateurs hold through stagnation; insiders engineer exits at the top.
quotes: In any field only the smart people can make fantastic money.

summary: New-year P&L showcase across multiple family and company accounts summing ~7.52 crore for 2020, with posted 2020 targets (PMS/hedge-fund AUM 100 crore, training fee 1 crore, trading income 5 crore). Predominantly self-referential screen-share of broker back-offices; salvageable only for the corporate-vs-personal taxation point and self-competition message.
lessons: F&O profits above ~5 crore in a personal account can fall into the ~42% effective slab while a corporate structure is taxed at ~25% - entity choice materially changes post-tax returns.
Compete only with your own past self; benchmarking against rivals distracts from process.
quotes: There is only one person with whom I want to compete and his name is P R Sundar.

summary: Bull-market arithmetic: price = EPS x PE. 2003-07 the Nifty rose ~7x on only ~30% PE expansion (20 to 26), i.e. earnings did the work. With 15-20% EPS compounding plus low-rate-driven PE expansion, a 4x move to 50,000 within five years is arithmetically possible; J-curve effects (IBC, NPA clean-up) support earnings.
lessons: Index price is EPS times PE: doubling EPS with doubling PE gives 4x - the 2003-07 bull was ~90% earnings-driven (PE only 20 to 26).
Low interest rates pull money from deposits into equities and drive PE expansion; high rates do the reverse.
Rupee stability (69 in 2013 to ~73 in 2020 vs 6 to 16 in 1978-86) removes a key reason for India-wide high rates.
Buy 10%+ corrections within a confirmed bull market; corrections of 10-30% occurred even inside the 2003-07 bull.
quotes: During the bull market, number one, earnings per share will increase. Number two, PE expansion will take place.

summary: 2020 closed above 14,000 (March low ~7,500). Record GST ₹1.15 lakh cr; strong auto sales (Tata Motors PV +84%). First-week-of-year direction theory (2011 example: −15% year). Risks: Georgia Senate runoffs, US jobs. PSU banks priced-for-bad argument (SBI/BoB). Range 13,800–14,200.
lessons: The first one or two weeks of January tend to set the year's tone (his empirical rule).
Negatives already in the price stop being negatives — PSU bank underperformance had priced in the bad news.

summary: Guided tour of the NSE option chain (strike grid, bid/ask, LTP, IV, volume, open interest) and first payoff-chart walkthroughs: long 13,200CE at 170 (premium 12,750, breakeven 13,370, max loss = premium, ~29% probability of profit) and long 12,800PE at 186 (breakeven 12,614). Covers lot sizes, weekly index expiries and illiquidity of long-dated options as of Dec 2020.
lessons: Breakeven at expiry = strike plus premium for calls, strike minus premium for puts; profit territory begins only beyond breakeven.
Maximum loss for an option buyer is the premium paid; profit is uncapped for calls.
Weekly expiries existed on Nifty and Bank Nifty while stock options had only the monthly expiry; long-dated (5-year) index options exist but are illiquid.
Probability of profit for a typical slightly-OTM long option is around 30% - buyers lose most of the time by design.

quotes: You cannot do the betting for one share. You have to do a betting for 75 shares.

summary: Gold framework for India: local price = international dollar price x USD/INR + import duty. Duty went 1% (pre-2013) to 10% (2013) to 12.5% (2020), incentivizing smuggling. Since 1973 gold has spiked only three times - 1980 oil crisis, 2008-11 Lehman era to $1,910, 2020 COVID to $2,070 - and mean-reverts once each crisis resolves; calls $3,000 unlikely, advising against gold as an investment.
lessons: Indian gold price decomposes into international price x exchange rate plus import duty - all three must be judged before a view.
Gold spikes only around global crises (1980, 2008-11, 2020) and stalls for years once the crisis resolves - crisis premiums mean-revert.
Import duties high enough (12.5%) incentivize smuggling, which caps further hikes - a policy constraint for the duty trajectory.
A stable rupee removes gold's currency-hedge argument for Indian investors.
quotes: As and when there is a global crisis prices shoot up, as and when the global crisis is resolved... prices come down or stay flat.

summary: V-shape recovery day (~350 points) after Janet Yellen urged more COVID relief - bulls outnumbered bears and shorts ran. Demonstrated hedged call-selling: 14,700+ calls sold pre-rally lost little, 14,000-14,200 PEs sold on the flip profited. Bajaj Finance and Kotak short-covering ahead of results.
lessons: Short covering is mechanical: when news flips, the weak side runs and the crowd joins the beating.
Sell calls into falls and puts into rallies symmetrically - VIX declines cushion reversals.

summary: GameStop/AMC short squeeze: retail Reddit crowd (WallStreetBets, ~4.5M members) forced hedge funds like Melvin Capital (reportedly -$5B) to cover; hedge funds sold other holdings to raise cash, creating a margin cascade that hit global markets; CBOE VIX jumped 63% in a day; Nifty -1,000 and Bank Nifty -3,000 in days; stay flat into the Feb 1 budget.
lessons: Short selling means selling shares you must borrow and return (SLB in India; borrowing in the US).
Hedge funds cover losses by selling other holdings - one squeeze can cascade into a whole-market margin call.
Low-float, heavily shorted names are ammunition for coordinated crowds; price can go 15x in two weeks.
When big institutions are endangered, exchanges and officials move to protect them - 'too big to fail' shapes crisis response.
quotes: Retail people came to know that these big funds have huge short positions... so we will buy these shares.

summary: Full event-strategy masterclass: 10 years of budget data show close-to-close moves under 2% (only exception -3.26% was COVID, not budget); weekly ATM straddle priced ~3.3% move; long straddle/strangle usually loses. Better: put/call back spreads (max loss ~Rs 20k vs Rs 32k) and put/call ratio spreads or butterflies for defined risk.
lessons: Implied volatility is almost always higher than historical volatility - paying full straddle premium around events is structurally losing.
Across 10 budgets, Nifty never closed more than 2% from the prior close except the COVID-coinciding 2020 budget (-3.26%).

Even across seven major crises (Lehman, Greece, taper tantrum, China devaluation, demonetization+Trump, Brexit, Feb-2018 US flash crash), Nifty never gapped more than 400 points except Lehman and COVID; Bank Nifty max 1,200.
Back spreads cut max loss by a third versus long straddles and win big only on large moves in one direction.

strategies.name: Put back spread
strategies.construction: sell 1x ATM+100 put; buy 2x ATM-200 puts (Nifty ~13,600: sell 13,700PE, buy 2x 13,400PE)
strategies.numbers: lower breakeven ~13,253 vs straddle's 13,162; max loss ~Rs 20,000 vs straddle ~Rs 32,000; margin ~Rs 1 lakh
strategies.best_regime: bearish into event; profits only on large falls
strategies.adjustments: roll or convert with far put
strategies.risks: sideways market loses the debit; margin understated by platforms

strategies.construction: sell 1x ATM-100 call; buy 2x ATM+200 calls
strategies.numbers: profit begins ~14,000 vs straddle 14,050; max loss ~Rs 20,000
strategies.best_regime: bullish into event
strategies.adjustments: same mirror logic
strategies.risks: small loss on big fall; sideways loses

strategies.name: Put ratio spread
strategies.construction: buy 1x ATM put (~Rs 175); sell 2x puts ~250-350 lower
strategies.numbers: max profit ~Rs 18,000-19,000 near 13,300-13,350; loss begins below ~13,100 and is uncapped; upside loss ~Rs 1,000
strategies.best_regime: mildly bearish; expects limited fall
strategies.adjustments: buy far OTM put to cap risk (butterfly)
strategies.risks: crash below short strikes = uncapped loss

quotes: The implied volatility is always higher than the historical volatility.

summary: ATH close; Bank Nifty +5,000 in four sessions (~16-17%); BSE market cap crossed ₹200 lakh crore. Compared Nirmala candle 1 (2019) vs 2 (2021): this day-3 sell-off was bought. Frog-experiment joke against media VIX misconceptions; future-spot premium convergence as exhaustion signal; SBI results triggered PSU rally (Indian Bank +15%).
lessons: When futures premium collapses to spot, the explosive phase is ending - expect consolidation, not continuation.
Judge data yourself; the media's VIX story (up = fall) is a misreading of fear.

summary: Why India is nearly immune to GameStop-style squeezes: illiquid SLB (lending income taxed as 'other sources'), circuit limits (Gitanjali Gems' lower-circuit cascade), SEBI's dynamic margins (Jet Airways 120%), market-wide position limits with 95% OI bans, and promoters would IPO into any spike. Plus semiconductor shortage hitting autos and 'very bad news is good news' jobs-data logic.
lessons: A GameStop squeeze is near-impossible in India: borrowing is illiquid, circuits halt cascades, SEBI raises margins dynamically, and position limits force bans.
Markets-wide position limit = 20% of free-float; at 95% OI a stock is banned from trading until OI falls below 80%.
Good news can be bad news and very bad news can be good - markets price stimulus expectations, not headlines.
Semiconductor shortages hit autos globally - supply chains, not demand, can cap cyclical rallies.
quotes: Good news is a good news, very good news is a bad news... very bad news is a good news, because people think the worst is over.

summary: Friday 26 Feb crash: Nifty −700+ intraday, Bank Nifty −2,000+; FII net −₹8,300 cr despite ~₹5,000 cr MSCI rebalancing inflows (gross >₹13,000 cr, possibly record). VIX ~30. GDP +0.4% beat-ish; J&J vaccine + House-passed $1.9tn stimulus. His put-ratio (buy 14,600 PE / sell 2× 14,000 PE). 50-DMA 14,400–450 bottom zone.
lessons: After a big crash the market needs hospital-rest before recovery — don't expect instant V-bounces.
OI is a guideline, not gospel — he faded the 14,000 PE support signal with a put ratio because his real risk line was 13,400.
High-VIX regimes are the option writer's harvest: far strikes still pay 4–5% a month.

summary: Recovery day: US $1.9T stimulus passed + J&J vaccine approval lifted Asia; gap-up held. Data checks: GST collections >Rs 1.1 lakh crore third straight month; India manufacturing PMI 57.5 vs China 50.7; India VIX crashed ~10%. Defines correction taxonomy (10% = normal pullback, 10-20% = correction, >20% = bear market) with 14,000-15,000 weekly range. Detours: opinion-poll tweet backlash and clubs/party joke.
lessons: Index falling >10% from peak is 'correction' territory; positioning and range maps beat headline fear.
Institutional flow tells (GST, PMI, rupee) separate sentiment dips from fundamental breaks.

summary: Fed's no-hike plus hawkish tone fell US; Brent entered bear territory below $70 (-20% from peak) - a big positive for India. OMCs, autos strong; Maruti +250 low-to-high. FII bought 600cr; DII sold 200cr. MF inflows ~15,000cr signaled retail maturity. Nifty held 10,500-10,600 for a 5th session; IIP/CPI/WPI due next week.
lessons: Retail SIP flows keep absorbing FII selling - flows matter more than headlines.

summary: Crude, crude, crude: Brent fell 7.5% - a 12th consecutive daily fall, unseen in 30 years - taking it 25% below $86.77 to under $65. India gains (OMCs, autos, banks via lower inflation) vs global growth fear. Nifty down, Bank Nifty up; Kotak -3% dented Bank Nifty 200 points intraday. Breakout or breakdown from 10,400-10,700 expected.
lessons: Huge two-way volatility between two levels usually resolves in a violent breakout.

summary: Argues index options beat stock options: indices cannot crash 50-60% in a day (DHFL -65%, Infibeam -70% did), index margins are half of stock margins for similar contract size, far-strike liquidity is deep, no physical delivery, panic exits always available.
lessons: Return on margin matters, not how much the underlying moves - index gives 6-7% on margin vs 4% for a stock moving twice as much
Stocks can gap 50-70% overnight; indices are circuit-protected
Index options keep liquidity in far strikes and later months; stock options do not
No physical delivery headache in index options
quotes: At the end of the day, what matters is the return on our investment. It is not how many percent the underlying moves.

summary: Explains Bharat Bond: a debt ETF holding only PSU bonds maturing before scheme maturity; 0.0005% expense (cheapest in India), 3-year and 10-year maturities, ~6.8%/7.6% indicative yields, 20% LTCG with indexation after 3 years, 5% collateral haircut, exchange-listed liquidity.
lessons: Falling interest-rate environments lift long-duration bond ETF prices - match duration to the rate view.
A 0.0005% expense ratio compounds into materially higher post-tax yield versus active debt funds.
Listed bond ETFs double as high-quality collateral (5% haircut), making idle capital productive for trading.

quotes: If interest rates in the economy go lower, these bonds will do very well; the day rates start rising, the premium will not look good.

summary: Post-rally consolidation view: support 9,900, resistance 10,700; Fed restricted bank buybacks (Dow -700 Friday); ITC results in line; data week ahead (auto sales, China/India PMI, US payrolls Thursday).
lessons: After a 1,000-point monthly rally, expect 1-2 weeks of range consolidation, not continuation.
Central-bank restrictions on one sector (bank buybacks) can drag the whole US tape overnight.

summary: Q&A batch: no fixed monthly returns as an option seller (HNI pattern: FD/debt-fund collateral is the primary income, trading is a bonus); margin shortfall penalty slabs; no safe strategy and no permanently strong company; minimum capital views; index fund vs futures; physical-delivery discipline; arbitrage vs reverse arbitrage on discounted futures.
lessons: Anchor option-selling expectations to collateral yield: primary income is interest on pledged debt funds; trading profit is supplementary and irregular.
Margin shortfall penalty: 0.5% of shortfall below 1 lakh, 1% above it, rising to 5% if the breach repeats beyond five sessions - never overtrade your collateral.
There is no safe strategy and no permanently fundamentally strong company - Reliance Communications/Infrastructure/Capital were once blue chips; understand risk and reward per strategy.
Squaring off stock-option positions before 3:30 pm on expiry avoids physical-delivery auction risk, especially in low-liquidity names.

strategies.name: Collateral-funded option selling (HNI pattern)
strategies.construction: Pledge debt mutual funds/bank FDs as collateral; sell options against the margin; keep interest as primary return
strategies.numbers: Stated pattern: 6-7% interest on debt funds while trading on pledged limit
strategies.best_regime: Wealthy, income-focused sellers who accept trading as a bonus stream
strategies.adjustments: Not applicable - structural allocation
strategies.risks: Trading losses eat the collateral cushion; interest is not guaranteed against credit events

strategies.name: Reverse arbitrage on futures discount
strategies.construction: Sell physical shares held in demat, buy the discounted futures; converge at expiry and reverse both
strategies.numbers: Example: stock 1000 spot vs 990 futures captures ~10 points
strategies.best_regime: Futures at significant discount (e.g., Nifty futures 80-90 points under spot)
strategies.adjustments: Hold to convergence
strategies.risks: Only works if shares already held; capital locked; convergence timing

quotes: stock market is not for the people who are expecting a regular or fixed return
there is no such thing called a safe strategy

summary: Q&A episode: expiry-day mechanics for hedged shorts (removing the long leg makes the short naked; index options cash-settle, stock options physically deliver if ITM - square off yourself); F&O ban-list illiquidity; advice to avoid stock F&O below ~1 crore capital and prefer indices; collateral eligibility (REC bonds, property, ELSS under 3 years ineligible); 50% cash margin component rule; Bharat Bond is cumulative, not annual-pay; option selling not advisable below ~10 lakh capital; no fixed timeline to become a successful trader.
lessons: Removing the protective long leg on expiry day converts your short into a naked position - margin and risk jump; close positions yourself rather than letting settlement decide.
Physical delivery applies only to stock F&O: short ITM call = give delivery, short ITM put = take delivery. Indices are cash-settled.
Collateral eligibility rule of thumb: anything not immediately liquidatable (property, REC/lock-in bonds, ELSS inside 3 years) cannot be pledged.
NSE margin rule: at least 50% of margin must be cash component - cash, FDs, liquid funds and Liquid BeES qualify; Bharat Bond counts as collateral, not cash.
quotes: Anything that cannot be liquidated immediately cannot be given as a collateral.

summary: Follow-up on the ITC call (bought ~198, now ~170, -15%): thesis unchanged - dividend yield above FD rates, effective cost cut below 170 by selling calls, patience and averaging down; high-dividend stocks are income plays, not momentum plays. New pick: BPCL - corrected from ~450-460 to ~350 on divestment delay; dividend yield ~4.65%; OMC earnings inversely track crude, and CME curves price crude flat (~$40-43) out to Dec 2022 and beyond. Entry paths: cash-secured puts (sold 350PE @14) or covered calls; full disclaimer.
lessons: Dividend-yield investing is a patience game: price declines raise the yield and attract institutions - the thesis strengthens as the price falls (if the dividend sustains).
Selling covered calls against a stock position lowers effective cost (bought ~198, effective <170) - income cushions drawdowns in non-momentum stocks.
Oil marketing companies profit inversely to crude: with CME curves flat near $40-43 out to 2022+, OMC earnings support is structural, not cyclical.
Event-delayed stocks (BPCL divestment) offer corrected entry points when the catalyst is deferred, not dead.

strategies.adjustments: Roll or take delivery and switch to covered calls
